en: One executor per base branch: <t1/>, <t2/> and <t3/> hold an exclusive lease at <t4/>, with the holder recorded. Holding it is holding an exclusive <t5/> on that file for the executor's life, so the kernel decides who holds it: of executors started at the same instant, in one checkout or in several worktrees of the repository, exactly one holds it and no pull request is merged twice. The integration unit tests race eight executors per round, and cases <n1/> and <n2/> race separate processes through the command line. A holder that ends, even by a crash, releases the lease at once; a live holder is never taken over. A record untouched for <n3/> minutes is reported stale to observers (<t6/>, <t7/>), which never take the lease. The executor renews its record before every observation, and a refresh keeps it fresh while the branch's derive runs. When the path no longer names the file the executor locked, or the record names another holder, the lease is lost: the drain stops as on any systemic failure (<t8/> exits <n4/>) and acts on nothing. The lease is taken for the base the forge was last observed to name, observed first when this checkout never asked, never for a guessed <t9/>.
